assertions.description: The event this change is about exists and carries the property it belongs to.
The other half of the change: a MediaQueryList dispatches change events, which is what puts a listener inside the rendering steps rather than in an ordinary task.

Both events are dispatched at the same step, and their order is fixed: run announces that a transition exists, start announces that its active interval has begun. A demo that measured the wrong one would report a delay that is really a delay value.
assertions.test: (async()=>{try{const h=document.createElement('div');h.style.cssText='position:absolute;left:-10000px;width:50px;height:50px;opacity:0.2;transition:opacity 300ms linear';document.body.append(h);const seen=[];const done=new Promise((resolve)=>{h.addEventListener('transitionrun',()=>{seen.push('run');});h.addEventListener('transitionstart',()=>{seen.push('start');resolve();});setTimeout(resolve,2000);});await new Promise((r)=>requestAnimationFrame(()=>requestAnimationFrame(r)));h.style.opacity='1';await done;h.remove();return seen[0]==='run'&&seen[1]==='start';}catch(e){return false;}})()

assertions.description: Within one rendering iteration, animations are updated and their events sent before the animation frame callbacks run. Every frame count in these demos rests on this ordering, so it is asserted rather than assumed.
assertions.test: (async()=>{try{const h=document.createElement('div');h.style.cssText='position:absolute;left:-10000px;width:50px;height:50px;opacity:0.2;transition:opacity 300ms linear';document.body.append(h);let frames=0;let at=null;const done=new Promise((resolve)=>{h.addEventListener('transitionrun',()=>{at=frames;resolve();},{once:true});setTimeout(resolve,2000);});await new Promise((r)=>requestAnimationFrame(()=>requestAnimationFrame(r)));h.style.opacity='1';const tick=()=>{frames+=1;if(frames<20&&at===null)requestAnimationFrame(tick);};requestAnimationFrame(tick);await done;h.remove();return at===0;}catch(e){return false;}})()

assertions.description: The feature itself. A transition created inside a media query change listener must have its transitionrun dispatched later in that same rendering iteration, so no animation frame callback runs in between. A count above zero is the deferral Chrome 153 removes.

assertions.description: The same requirement for the other event dispatched inside the rendering steps: a transition created in a scroll handler must not wait for the next iteration either.
assertions.test: (async()=>{try{const h=document.createElement('div');h.style.cssText='position:absolute;left:-10000px;width:60px;height:60px;overflow:auto';const inner=document.createElement('div');inner.style.cssText='height:300px';const panel=document.createElement('div');panel.style.cssText='width:20px;height:20px;opacity:0.2;transition:opacity 300ms linear';inner.append(panel);h.append(inner);document.body.append(h);let frames=0;let at=null;const done=new Promise((resolve)=>{h.addEventListener('scroll',()=>{panel.addEventListener('transitionrun',()=>{at=frames;resolve();},{once:true});panel.style.opacity='1';const tick=()=>{frames+=1;if(frames<20&&at===null)requestAnimationFrame(tick);};requestAnimationFrame(tick);},{once:true});setTimeout(resolve,3000);});await new Promise((r)=>requestAnimationFrame(()=>requestAnimationFrame(r)));h.scrollTop=40;await done;h.remove();return at===0;}catch(e){return false;}})()
